newsitem.title: USA: CBOT rice closes lower on setback, volume trimmed.
newsitem.headline: CBOT rice closes lower on setback, volume trimmed.

text.p: CBOT rice futures closed lower on a setback Monday after contract highs were set Friday in response to an active weekly export sales number, traders said.
"The market was taking a breather from the past week's active trade," a trader said.
USDA Friday said U.S. rice exports for the week ended January 16, totaled 120,900 tonnes, about twice as much as expectations for 60,000 to 65,000 tonnes.
Traders were skeptical of news Monday that Iraq will tender February 3 for 30,000 tonnes of U.S. long grain rice. U.S. exporters characterized the tender as very unusual.
Rice futures volume, according to the CBOT, dropped to 300 contracts from Friday's level of 767 contracts.
Rice closed 1/2 cent to six cents per cwt lower, with March down 1-1/2 at $11.88.
